This projection mechanism creates a dualism between the subjective origin and objective appearance of sensations. The sensory projection isomorphism maps neural activity to perceived spatial positions, while the veridical hallucination kernel emerges when this projection coincides with real-world stimuli. Neural spatial mapping further formalizes how cortical representations assign apparent locations to sensations.
